tagline.text: A 1 km white-sand beach and sunset spot in Saavedra, Moalboal

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,000 (entry, environmental fee, transport and food, per person per day)

children.text: Basdaku White Beach is a white-sand beach more than 1 km long in the village of Saavedra in Moalboal, southwest Cebu. It is known for shallow, calm water and west-facing sunsets, and at about 6 km from Panagsama Beach it is a good place to rest between sardine-run snorkeling and dive days.

Basdaku Beach is a beach in the village of Saavedra in Moalboal, on the southwest of Cebu Island, and is commonly called White Beach. Basdaku is Cebuano for "big sand," a name said to come from a shoreline that runs more than 1 km. Soft white sand stretches long against a backdrop of palm trees, and it is described as a beach that Moalboal visitors drop into between dive days.
It is about
6 km
north of Panagsama Beach, roughly
15 minutes

by tricycle. If Panagsama is the base for diving and sardine-run snorkeling, Basdaku suits soaking in the sea, resting and watching the sunset. The water faces west across the Tañon Strait toward Negros Oriental, so the view at dusk is described as lovely.

The water is described as shallow and calm, deepening gradually. Because the bottom is sand, there are said to be no sudden drop-offs or strong currents close to shore, so families with children visit often. For reef snorkeling, however, Panagsama or Pescador Island is better, and sources disagree on whether shore snorkeling is possible at Basdaku, so lower your expectations. Small tide pools appear at low tide.

Facilities are simple rather than resort-grade. Along the beach road there are small eateries and sari-sari stores, cottages and mats for rent, and a small entrance fee is collected at the gate. The fee is collected in cash at the village kiosk and amounts differ slightly between sources, so confirm the latest rate locally. On weekend afternoons it is crowded with families from Cebu City, and weekday afternoons are much quieter.

blocks.title: A white-sand beach over 1 km long

children.text: Soft white sand runs long along a shoreline lined with palm trees. Wide, fine-sand beaches are uncommon in Moalboal, so it is well suited to strolling, walking and photos.

The water is described as clear and shallow, deepening gradually. Compared with Panagsama's rocky shore, it is much easier for weak swimmers and children. Still, children need an adult with them, and depth changes with the tide, so check locally.

The beach faces west, so sunset is the main draw. The usual advice is to arrive about an hour before sunset, claim a spot, and wait at the water's edge or at a cottage. Sunset time varies by season, from about 5:30 p.m. in December to about 6:40 p.m. in June.

If you need shade, you can rent a cottage on the beach. Rental prices are described as ranging widely, from ₱100 to ₱2,500 depending on size and location, and mats run about ₱100–200. Most places are said to allow outside food, so check when you book.

Eateries and small stores along the road to the beach sell grilled seafood, rice and drinks. Some places are said to have grill stations, and prices are local prices. Check exact menus and prices locally.
One source says kayaks and paddleboards can be rented for about ₱200–300 per hour. Availability and prices vary from day to day, so confirm on site.

It is a good place to stop and rest on an afternoon after diving or sardine-run snorkeling at Panagsama. Enjoying the water early in the morning, then resting at Basdaku and watching the sunset, is a popular day.

Panagsama has a shore of rock and coral fragments, so many people wear water shoes to enter and the water gets deep right off the edge. At Basdaku you wade in slowly from a sand beach, so the feel is different even within Moalboal. Combining the two on the same day balances activity and rest. The two beaches are about 6 km apart, so allow time to travel between them.
From your lodging in Panagsama, set out for Basdaku by tricycle or motorcycle. It takes about
12–15 minutes
Pay the entrance fee (about
) at the gate kiosk, along with the environmental fee (about
) if you have not yet paid it.
Pick a shaded cottage or spread a mat and swim.
Have an early dinner of grilled seafood and rice at a roadside eatery.
About an hour before sunset, go down to the water's edge and wait for the sunset. The western sky is open, which is great for photos.
Arrange your ride back before it gets dark. The road is dark after sunset.
Arrange your return tricycle in advance or hire a motorcycle taxi to wait. Vehicles become scarce after dark.

items.title: A Moalboal day
items.subtitle: Sardine run and a sunset beach

children.text: Snorkel the sardine run or dive at Panagsama Beach. Early morning is best, with fewer people.
Return to your lodging for breakfast and a rest.
Head to Basdaku for lunch and beach time.
Watch the sunset and leave before it gets dark.
The environmental fee is described as paid only once a day, so keep your receipt.
There are flights from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB). Check airline notices for flights.
From the airport, take a taxi or ride-hailing car to the South Bus Terminal in Cebu City.
Take a bus to Moalboal from the South Bus Terminal. Routes via Barili or Badian are described, and the trip takes about
3 hours
. An air-conditioned bus is described at about
, and ordinary buses are said to be cheaper.
Vans are also an option. Get off in Moalboal town or near Panagsama.
A tricycle hired for the whole vehicle from Panagsama is described at
, or
per seat. Tell the driver "White Beach" or "Basdaku."
A motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) is described at about
per person, and a scooter rental at about
per day.
If you drive, parking at the entrance is described at around ₱50 for a car and ₱20 for a motorcycle.
Basdaku is most comfortable in the dry season, when the weather is settled. The sea is calm and the sunsets tend to be clear, so
November–May
is best. In the rainy season, rain and wind can make swimming conditions worse.

Within a day, early afternoon to sunset is the most popular window and it gets crowded on weekends. To avoid crowds, go on a weekday afternoon or early in the morning. At low tide small tide pools appear, which children enjoy.

items.note: Large differences by size and location

children.text: Prices are approximate as of

There are small resorts and cottages close to Basdaku, but most travelers stay in Panagsama, the base for diving and snorkeling, or in Moalboal town, and come for a half-day visit. Panagsama has far more lodging choices.

Small eateries and stores along the beach road sell grilled seafood, rice and drinks. Many sources say outside food and drinks are allowed, but rules differ by cottage. Facilities are simple, so bring water and snacks. The nearest ATMs are described as being in Moalboal town and on Panagsama's main road, so get cash in advance.

Whether to rent a cottage depends on your group. For a short rest for two, a mat and the shade of a tree are enough, while a family or group of friends staying half a day is better off with a large cottage with a table. One source puts a large cottage at about ₱1,000, but it varies by day and spot, so ask the price first and negotiate. A few lodgings are said to be near the beach, but prices and quality change often, so check booking sites or local information.
Everything is paid in cash, so bring plenty of small change. Entrance, the environmental fee, parking and tricycles are all cash, so it helps to set aside small bills.
If you want the sunset, arrive about an hour before it. Sunset time changes by season.
If you already paid the environmental fee in Panagsama, show your receipt. It is described as once a day.
If reef snorkeling is your goal, choose Panagsama or Pescador Island over Basdaku.
There is little shade, so bring sunscreen, a hat and water.
Weekend afternoons are crowded; weekdays and early afternoons are quieter.
Tent and camping rules differ by source and may not be permitted, so book lodging for overnight stays.
After dark, rides become scarce and the road is dark, so return before sunset.
Before going into the water, leave your shoes and bag somewhere visible close to your cottage or mat.
Fees and camping rules are set by the village kiosk and individual operators and change from time to time. Check the latest notice on site.
The sea is described as shallow and calm, but it varies with tide and weather, so children should always be watched by an adult.
Rocks and tide pools exposed at low tide can be slippery and sharp, so wear water shoes.
Facilities are not resort-grade, so toilets and showers may be basic.
Do not leave valuables on a cottage or mat while you swim.
Information differs between sources. Check entrance and facility fees again locally.
Panagsama Beach in
Moalboal
, known for sardine-run snorkeling and diving, is about
6 km
from Basdaku.
Kawasan Falls
, south of Moalboal, is famous for canyoneering and its blue falls, and many people combine it with a trip here.
A small island off Panagsama described as a snorkeling and diving spot.
Osmeña Peak
, the highest peak on Cebu, is popular for its sunrise views and is sometimes added to a day itinerary.
